section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Gravity Fitness Signs 23K-SF Lease at Queens’ Flushing Plaza: An athletic club is following a gravitational pull leading it to eastern Queens. Gravity Fitness signed a long-term, 23,000-square-foot lease at Muss Development ’s Flushing Plaza at 41-61 Kissena Boulevard , where it will occupy the ground floor of a two-story office and retail complex in Downtown Flushing, according.

BankUnited Lands Fifth Avenue Retail Flagship and Expands Offices at 450 Park Avenue: BankUnited is not only landing on Fifth Avenue with a new flagship branch, but it’s also expanding its office space along Park Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The Florida-based bank signed a retail lease for 10,068 square feet on the south corner of Amazon ’s tower at 452 Fifth Avenue , also known as 10.

Burlington Stores Inks 32K SF at Brooklyn Navy Yard’s Admiral’s Row Campus: Burlington Stores is coming to the Brooklyn Navy Yard. The retailer formerly known as Burlington Coat Factory signed a 31,717-square-foot retail lease at 25 Navy Street , according to city records filed Tuesday evening.

Chinese Restaurant Chain to Open 10K-SF Eatery at 365 West 46th Street: One thing New York City does not lack is a place to find great Chinese food, and New Yorkers are about to get another spot to add to their lists. Nong Geng Ji , one of China’s most popular Hunan cuisine brands, has inked a 9,900-square-foot retail lease at 365 West 46th Street in Manhattan’s Hell’s Kitchen.
section_overviews.cre_daily:

Arlington Redevelopment Gains Steam Near DFW Sports Hub: Trademark Property started construction this summer on the $135M-plus rebuild of Lincoln Square into Anthem, a 404K SF walkable retail and entertainment center with 10 tenants signed and completion expected in early 2028.

Manhattan Retail Availability Hits Record Low as Banks Expand: Average availability across Manhattan’s prime retail corridors dropped to 11.4% in Q3 2026, the lowest reading since JLL began tracking in 2017, with only 157 spaces left. Bank of America, OceanFirst and Citibank signed leases totaling nearly 35,000 square feet, and JLL says many more bank deals are pending, adding.

Miami Retail Pipeline Hits 1.3M SF, Highest Since Early 2023: Miami-Dade’s retail pipeline reached 1.3M SF in the third quarter, double last year’s level, as developers gain confidence in a market with 3% direct vacancy. Leasing slowed to 257K SF across 118 deals from 413K SF across 150 deals in Q2, and absorption turned negative, yet triple-net asking rents set a record $44.34.
section_overviews.new_york_post:
BXP’s 343 Madison Ave. tower is going up: Marquee-name tenants have already been signed for about half of the building’s 930,000 square feet -- insurance giant Starr and law firm McDermott Will & Schulte.

Former Olympian accused of refusing to leave $26K-a-month NYC luxe condo as owners fight to evict her: Owners say the ex-luger overstayed her lease and sank a $6.75 million deal at star-studded 150 Charles Street.

Michael Dell-backed firm’s $875M bet in Boca Raton is paying off as $9M condos get snapped up: Roughly 40% of the 75 homes were claimed within months at the century-old resort, which has never sold residences on its grounds before.

Chrysler Trylons are for sale, too: The Chrysler Building’s storefronts remain depressingly empty on both Lexington Avenue and East 42nd Street except for a Chase bank branch.

items.headline: Record Diesel Prices Squeeze Retail Development Pipeline
items.summary: Diesel averaged $6.38 per gallon on Sept. 28, up from about $3.81 in late February, adding to construction and supply-chain costs for retail developers and retailers. Just over 60M SF of retail is under construction, 4% above the all-time low CoStar has recorded, while JLL put Q2 vacancy at 4.4% and net absorption at 10.2M SF. Retailers such as Aldi, Burlington, TJ Maxx and Dollar Tree plan large store expansions, but flat rents and rising costs mean limited new supply to absorb them.…

Fairbourne and AEW are modernizing the 747K SF Arlington Highlands, which only recently slipped below 96% leased, while opportunity zones along Collins Street target the gap between downtown and the stadiums.…

items.headline: British Luxury Fashion Brand JW Anderson to Open at SoHo’s 138 Wooster Street
items.summary: British luxury fashion label JW Anderson has leased 4,500 square feet at 138 Wooster Street in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood for its first stand-alone U.S. store, Commercial Observer has learned. Founded in 2008 by Jonathan Anderson — the newly appointed creative director of Dior and a two-time British Fashion Awards Designer of the Year recipient — the influential fashion label is staking out a claim in a highly sought-after part of SoHo at a time when quality retail space in the neighborhood is increasingly…

items.headline: Miami Retail Pipeline Hits 1.3M SF, Highest Since Early 2023
items.summary: Miami-Dade’s retail pipeline reached 1.3M SF in the third quarter, double last year’s level, as developers gain confidence in a market with 3% direct vacancy. Leasing slowed to 257K SF across 118 deals from 413K SF across 150 deals in Q2, and absorption turned negative, yet triple-net asking rents set a record $44.34 per SF. Heavy preleasing is letting developers underwrite new projects, but vacancy below 3% in core submarkets means tenants must stay flexible to find space.…

items.headline: Charter School Inks 56K-SF Lease in Retail Center Near Miami Suburb
items.summary: Charter school network BridgePrep Academy will open another location, this time inside a shopping center in Miami-Dade County. The school operator, which has 19 locations across Florida, signed a 56,000-square-foot lease at the open-air California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, near Aventura, 15 miles north of Downtown Miami. The 273,050-square-foot property, owned by RK Centers , sits west of Interstate 95 at 750 Ives Dairy Road .…

items.headline: Luxury Spending Falls 6%, Raising Risks for High-End Retail
items.summary: Citi says U.S. luxury credit card spending fell 6% year over year in September, after 4% declines in both July and August, challenging a source of strength for luxury retail. Higher earners drive demand: Moody’s Analytics found households earning about $250,000 or more account for 49.7% of consumer spending, up from roughly 36% three decades earlier. The data does not show falling rents or occupancy yet, but landlords with luxury tenants have reason to watch tenant performance as consumer confidence weakens.…

items.headline: Retail Sales Jump 6% in August, Boosting CRE Property Demand
items.summary: Retail sales rose 6% year-over-year in August 2026 and have averaged 5.2% growth year-to-date, a pace historically uncommon outside post-recession recoveries. Households remain financially healthy overall, as rising incomes and record savings offset auto, credit card and household debt sitting at or near record highs. items.summary: Three women’s apparel brands have taken office and showroom space at 231 West 39th Street in Manhattan’s Garment District, landlord broker and building manager Adams & Company announced Wednesday. items.summary: Lower Manhattan’s South Street Seaport will be living la dolce vita with its latest restaurant lease. items.summary: Luxury French fashion house Yves Saint Laurent will open a new store at 717 Fifth Avenue , a new report revealed. Saint Laurent is currently at 3 East 57th Street , where it opened in 2003.…

items.headline: South Beach’s Cameo Theater Could Reopen With Romain Zago Concept
items.summary: Nightlife operator Romain Zago wants to reopen the historic Cameo Theater in South Beach seven years after its nightclub shuttered. Zago, who made a name for himself owning the nearby Mynt Lounge nightclub, has filed plans to turn the Art Deco theater at 1445 Washington Avenue into a 466-seat restaurant and lounge. The plans call for a bar and lounge with 226 seats on the ground floor, with the existing stage remaining. The second floor will house a 240-seat restaurant.…
